MEMORANDUM
  Agenda Item #:  9
  Meeting Date: July 27, 2021

TO:  HONORABLE MAYOR AND CITY COUNCIL MEMBERS

THRU:  LAURA GUGLIELMO, CITY MANAGER

FROM:  CAROLYNN PETRU, INTERIM PUBLIC WORKS DIRECTOR

SUBJECT:  RECOMMENDATIONS OF THE PARKLANDS COMMITTEE
  FOR JULY 8, 2021

DATE:  JULY 27, 2021

ACTION REQUIRED  CONSENT  X  RECEIVE & FILE

Recommendation

It is recommended that the City Council approve the actions of the Parklands Committee
for the meeting of July 8, 2021.

Summary

At the Parklands Committee meeting of July 8, 2021, all committee members were
present. Two applications were discussed and there was no communication from the
public.

Analysis and Findings

The City held a Parklands Committee meeting on July 8, 2021 and the Committee
recommended the following actions to be approved by the City Council.

1. PC-554-21; Application to remove six Eucalyptus located in the Cataluna Strip
  behind 1617 through 1641 Cataluna Place

  Applicant: Sulabha and Anil Dave, 2249 Via Cerritos, Palos Verdes Estates, CA
  90274

  1
 Staff introduced this application as a request to remove six Eucalyptus trees for view
restoration (Attachment A). The application had been continued from the May 13, 2021
Parklands Committee meeting in order to provide adequate notice to the affected
homeowners.

Staff indicated the trees are all located in the Parklands behind 1617 through 1641
Cataluna Place and the applicant has resided on the street above at 2249 Via Cerritos for
the last 40 years. Four of the Eucalyptus tree are approximately 75 feet tall with a
collective width of 200 feet. These four tall Eucalyptus trees (Nos. 1, 2, 5, & 6) encroach
into the view of the Santa Monica Bay, partial Queens’s necklace coastline, city lights,
Malibu hills and Blue Ocean. The two smaller Eucalyptus (Nos. 3 & 4) are not
encroaching into the view. The trees were trimmed in 2017 and are currently safe and
healthy.

Staff identified the following options to improve the applicant’s view:

  •  Standard trimming of all six trees.
  •  Trimming and topping the four tall trees by 15-20 feet (Tree Nos. 1, 2, 5 & 6).
  •  Removal of Tree No. 1 and Tree No. 5, with trimming and topping of the other
  two tall trees (Tree Nos. 2 & 6).
  •  Removal of all four tall trees (Tree Nos. 1, 2, 5 & 6).

It should be noted that none of the options would completely restore the applicant’s view.
In addition, any tree removal would create a reduction in privacy and the neighborhood
character would be damaged if all the tall trees were removed.

A considerable number of letters of opposition were received from the residents on
Cataluna Place and other parts of the community listing numerous reasons that removal
of healthy trees for the view should not be approved. These letters indicated any removal
will affect the neighborhood character, will create privacy issues, will expose an
unattractive view of the hillside, will reduce the screening of the large homes on Via
Cerritos, and would be harmful to the environment that provides cooling shade and a
home for wildlife. Many of these residents reiterated their written comments at the
meeting, and also indicated that the applicant should have known the trees would grow to
block the view when they purchased their home.

During the time from the continuance of the May hearing to the July hearing, a meeting
with the applicants and a few residents of Cataluna Place was held. No compromise or
agreement could be reached between the parties.

The Committee members all agreed the application was difficult to balance and the view
could not be restored even if all six trees were removed. Any removal would affect
privacy, change the neighborhood character and would be inadequate to address the
applicant’s request. The volume of opposition to not modify the neighborhood character,
privacy and the amenities the trees provided were factors that were more important than
view restoration.
  2
 Committee member Cooper motioned, second by Committee member Rossick, to
recommend to the City Council to deny the application and require a safety inspection of
Tree No. 1 located behind 1617 Cataluna Place by the Urban Forester to determine the
safety of this tree. The vote was unanimously in favor (5-0).

2. PC-556-21; Application to remove three Brazilian pepper trees and one Silver Dollar
  Eucalyptus located in the parkway adjacent to 877 Rincon Lane, reduce the height of
  the hedges behind 865 and 869 Rincon Lane, and remove three branches on the
  Eucalyptus tree adjacent to 881 Rincon Lane

  Applicant: Marilyn Radford, 900 Via Nogales, Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

  Staff introduced this application for removal of three Brazilian pepper trees and one
  silver dollar Eucalyptus tree, topping a number of hedges and trimming a few
  branches on a distant Eucalyptus as a view enhancement request. The applicant
  resides across the street at 900 Via Nogales and some of the trees block the view of
  the Blue Ocean, partial Queen’s Necklace, coastline and city lights views from the
  main viewing areas in the home. The hedge at 865 Rincon Lane is blocking view
  from the upstairs bedroom along with the distant Eucalyptus adjacent to 881 Rincon
  Lane that narrows the view corridor of the coastline.

  Staff indicated removal of the Silver Dollar Eucalyptus adjacent to 877 Rincon Lane
  is not recommended by staff as the view can be enhanced by trimming to see under
  the canopy. The Brazilian pepper trees would not be able to be elevated high enough
  to see under and require removal to improve the view in an effective way. The
  neighborhood character is the Canary Island Date palm which lines Rincon Lane and
  the Brazilian peppers are not the designated street tree and never were.

  Staff identified the hedge behind 865 Rincon Lane as a non-standard encroachment
  that exceeds the allowable height of shrubs in the parkway and adds to view
  blockage. This is also true for shrubs/trees behind 869 Rincon Lane, but the existing
  hedges are smaller than the trees on private property and will only block the view in
  the future if allowed to grow. The applicant requests to control the height of the
  hedges behind these two properties on Rincon Lane to not exceed the fence height.
  The shrubs at 865 Rincon Lane may provide privacy for this address but privacy can’t
  be obtained by planting tall hedges in the public parkway and is a violation of the
  Palos Verdes Estates Municipal Code and public works standards for parkway which
  limits planting height to 30 inches tall.

  The Large Eucalyptus in the parkway adjacent to 881 Rincon Lane is 460 feet away
  from the applicant’s property and is requested for a few branches to be removed to
  widen the view corridor. This will not harm the tree and could improve safety.

  The applicant spoke indicating the view of the coastline, Queen’s Necklace and Blue
  Ocean was obscured for her and a number of the adjacent neighbors. The owners of
  the home above the applicant at 905 Via Del Monte supported all the requested

  3
   removals and indicated view and safety concerns with Silver Dollar Eucalyptus tree
  adjacent to 877 Rincon Lane.

  Committee member Nye ask about the Committee’s options concerning the
  encroaching fence at 869 Rincon Lane and replanting the designated street tree to
  replace the Brazilian peppers. Staff indicated removal of the fence is not part of the
  application and is a Code Enforcement issue. New trees can be planted as a condition
  of approval for the removal of three Brazilian peppers, but is normally a response to a
  request from the adjacent owner of 877 Rincon Lane using the funds from the ‘Tree
  Bank’. Requiring payment of $1,500 is a requirement that is optional when approving
  non-designated street trees for removal.

  Committee member Nye motioned, second by Committee member Rossick, to
  approve the application as recommended in the staff report: Recommend approval to
  the City Council to remove three Brazilian pepper trees located in the parkway
  adjacent to 877 Rincon Lane according to the ‘Standard Conditions for Tree Removal
  Approvals’ and deny the removal of the Silver Dollar Eucalyptus tree adjacent to 877
  Rincon Lane. Require removal of the stumps, payment of $1,500 to the ‘Tree Bank’
  and a ‘Tree Removal’ permit. Approve annual trimming of the hedges adjacent to 865
  and 869 Rincon Lane to 30-inches in height. Approve removal of 3 branches on the
  Eucalyptus tree adjacent to 881 Rincon Lane with a permit from the City and at the
  direction of the Urban Forester.

The meeting was adjourned at 9:30 PM to September 9, 2021.

Notification

These matters have been agenized and posted in the routine manner.

Carl Moritz
Urban Forester
